solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Blissful round for a copper, if in charge

parts.note: a police officer's regular round is the beat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer is delighted to be given a patrol, provided they are in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatific describes a look of saintly happiness, a close synonym for blissful.

clue.text: Man? One finally asleep in suitable location

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for the place

parts.note: a bed is the suitable place for someone asleep
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: picks the closing letter of asleep

explanation.surface: A man who is finally asleep is in the right place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and P (the last letter of asleep) inside BED. The question mark flags man as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two legs, so a man is an example of a two-footed animal.

clue.text: What you may do when you have a cold is vulgar

definitions.text: What you may do when you have a cold
definitions.meaning: a blocked nose dulls the palate, so you sense flavour to a smaller degree

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is how a cold dulls flavour; as one it means lacking refinement.

clue.text: Found holding Bible — gets absolved

indicators.note: the outer word contains the other

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it, as to forge does
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a group around the Bible and finds forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' means to cast metal, not discovered; 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgive someone is to absolve them of blame, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Sell more than anyone else, as a convenience shop might?

definitions.meaning: to dominate a trade by controlling its supply
a local shop on a street corner occupies the corner of the trading area

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means gaining control of a trade; a corner shop literally sits at the market's corner.

clue.text: Eleanor in front of company is uncontrollable nag

indicators.note: says the first piece comes before the second in the answer

parts.note: Eleanor Bron is an English actress, so her surname stands in for the first name

explanation.surface: Someone called Eleanor, at the head of a business, is an uncontrollable nag at her staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleanor Bron is a British actress and comedian; the clue uses her first name to point at her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an untamed or half-broken horse, and a nag is a horse, so an unruly one fits.

clue.text: A certain John given bread is tucking in time and time again

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll in Britain

indicators.note: the word is is placed between the two letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, used again
T is the abbreviation for time, used again
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called John, handed a roll, keeps eating it over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking in' signals the word is going between the two Ts, one for each 'time'; a bap is a soft British bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: John the Baptist is the biblical figure known for baptising, so he is a particular John.

clue.text: English dish at home served up with salt

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish
in means at home

explanation.surface: A British pudding eaten at home comes with seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses E + TART + IN, giving the answer from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid, used in fertilisers.

clue.text: Had too much dinner maybe — or even tea possibly!

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuffed after dinner, or perhaps even after tea.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can be an evening meal, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overeaten is to have consumed too much food, as at a dinner.

clue.text: Sailor initially protected by less crude officer on ship

indicators.note: the outer word guards the letter set within it

parts.note: something less crude is purer, more refined

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is shielded by a more refined officer aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts S, the first letter of Sailor, inside PURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A purser is the officer responsible for accounts and passengers aboard a ship.

clue.text: Witty conversation about some leaders with extravagant expectations

parts.note: RE is Latin for concerning, a standard crossword sense of about
part means some of, a portion

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, here of extravagant and expectations

explanation.surface: Banter about certain bosses who hope for far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, clever back-and-forth talk, which is witty conversation.

clue.text: Georgia's brought in to take out agent

indicators.note: Georgia's letters are inserted into the other word

parts.note: to delete is to take out or remove
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: Georgia has brought in someone to eliminate a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a representative acting for others, which is an agent.

clue.text: Like a mad person swimming through Paris, as you'd say

indicators.note: signals the phrase is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: anyone swimming through Paris is in the Seine, the river that runs through the city

explanation.surface: Only a lunatic would go swimming through the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as you'd say' turns IN SEINE (in the river through Paris) into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Insane means mad, so it describes how a mad person is.

clue.text: Stiff covering about to be sealed in adhesive

indicators.note: says one piece is enclosed within another

parts.note: cement is an adhesive, a glue
RE is Latin for concerning, a standard crossword sense of about

explanation.surface: A rigid casing is about to be stuck fast with glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' is slang for a corpse, so a stiff covering is a shroud, not something rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: A cerement is a waxed cloth for wrapping the dead, a shroud for a corpse.

clue.text: Speaks against poetry

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
verses are lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone argues against poems.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk with someone, so converses means speaks.

clue.text: Engineers put in that warning

indicators.note: the engineers' letters are placed inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers installed that alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a warning of harm to come.

clue.text: Being bitter or sour can seem awful

indicators.note: seem awful suggests things look a mess, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Feeling resentful or sour can look terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of bitter, lasting resentment.

clue.text: Old statesman making certain assertions, incompletely recorded here

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A politician of the past makes assertions he is sure of, only partly captured in this report.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of certain and the start of assertions; 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamal Abdel Nasser was the Egyptian president who died in 1970, an old statesman.

clue.text: Good person left to eat coarse bit of food

indicators.note: the outer letters swallow the other word

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
rude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A virtuous person is left to consume a rough morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good person' is the crossword convention for a saint; 'to eat' signals the coarse word going between the saint and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A strudel is a pastry of thin dough rolled around a filling, an item of food.

clue.text: As pragmatic person, ease up about Muslim

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the other

parts.note: to rest is to ease up
Ali is a common Muslim name, as with the cousin of the Prophet

explanation.surface: Being practical, someone relaxes on the subject of a follower of Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the outer word going around the name; 'As' is a link word, and 'ease up' is a verb, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they are, which is a practical, pragmatic outlook.

clue.text: Capital noted for being frantic around first working day?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation for the weekday
frantic means wildly agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
Monday, abbreviated MON, starts the working week

explanation.surface: A city famous for its frenzied Monday mornings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' looks like a plain verb but is anagram fodder, scrambled by 'frantic'; 'around' wraps the result about the weekday abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital city of the Canadian province of Alberta.

clue.text: Sounds like military escort

indicators.note: says one word is pronounced like another

parts.note: martial means relating to war or the military

explanation.surface: It is said to resemble a soldier's guard.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal people is to guide or usher them, as an escort does.

clue.text: Mistakes awfully rare by army

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: The armed forces seldom get things wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges RARE to ERRA; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, especially those listed in a printed book.

clue.text: Tune to broadcast, going well over our heads?

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
taken as written
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A melody to be put out on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a missile fired from one aircraft at another travels high above us.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-to-air weapons fly between aircraft, literally far above the heads of people on the ground.

clue.text: Some ditherer unlikely to perform again

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dithering person is not likely to give another show.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerun a show or race is to stage or run it again.

clue.text: Buddy bringing excitement to team

indicators.note: the excitement is attached to the end of the team word

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a kick is a thrill or bit of excitement

explanation.surface: A friend who livens up the squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, a buddy.

clue.text: Clean President

definitions.meaning: to vacuum a carpet, from the brand of vacuum cleaner
Herbert ... was the 31st President of the United States

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a US president is also a British verb for vacuuming.

clue.text: Axeman finally coming in to divide a piece of wood

indicators.note: the letter enters the middle of the other word

parts.note: to split is to divide

indicators.note: picks the closing letter of axeman

explanation.surface: A woodcutter arrives at last to chop a log in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts N, the last letter of Axeman, inside SPLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A splint is a thin strip of wood, such as one used to support a broken limb.

clue.text: Charm of fantastic A-list fellow

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: The appeal of a marvellous celebrity guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges ALIST to TALIS; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring good luck, a lucky charm.
